description:
LOW PRIORITY, FUTURE (USER 2026-09-02: "write up as a low prio task for sometime in the future").  NOT scheduled; do not start unasked.  REWRITTEN s465 after the USER discussion: this is PART (b) -- the USER-SUPPLIED hints; part (a), exporting what the compiler already KNOWS, is #1035 and comes first (the hints reuse its vocabulary).

USER ASK: "(optionally?) add some modification to variable declarations or something, to specify when a variable or sub parameter just contain integers, numbers or strings.  So it is visible in the IR."  Confirmed intent (USER): annotate what variables are used for, so a second backend (C/C++/JS) can compile from the IR.

WHY A HINT IS NEEDED AT ALL: inference (VarAnnotator, the Kind-A raw emissions in Pl/Passes.pm) is blind at (a) a CALL boundary -- a sub parameter is whatever the caller passes; (b) aggregate ELEMENTS (no per-container family is inferred); (c) anything the analyser gives up on (escaping cells, string evals).  A hint is a fact the compiler did not have to prove.

TWO CANDIDATE SPELLINGS (decision OPEN; the USER asked 2026-09-02 "we could have different variable declarations for different types?" -- i.e. leaning to spelling 2):
  1. ATTRIBUTE on the existing declarator:  `my $i :int = 0;`  `my @a :int;`  `our $s :str;`
     + valid perl SYNTAX as-is; PPI already lexes a Token::Attribute on `my`/`our`/`state`; covers all three declarators; sub parameters via a SUB attribute (`sub f :types(int,str) ($x, $y)` -- 5.40 signatures take no per-param attributes) or the `my ($x,$y) = @_` body form directly.
     - real perl dies "Invalid SCALAR attribute: int" unless a MODIFY_SCALAR_ATTRIBUTES handler is in scope -> a tiny `lib/PCL/types.pm` shim exporting no-op MODIFY_{SCALAR,ARRAY,HASH}_ATTRIBUTES makes perl accept the file (right layer, CLAUDE.md 9a: the shim is data, "an attribute on a declaration is a fact" is the generic mechanism).
  2. DISTINCT DECLARATORS:  `int $i = 0;`  `num $x;`  `str $s = "";`  (or capitalised `Int $i`)
     + reads like a typed language; the type is the first word of the declaration, the IR reader and the human see the same thing.
     - NOT valid perl as a declaration: real perl needs a SOURCE-FILTER shim (`use PCL::types;` via Filter::Simple rewriting `int $i` -> `my $i` etc.) to run the file at all.  `int` is a perl BUILTIN (truncation): `int $x;` is legal perl today and `int $x = 5;` parses as `int($x = 5)`, so the lowercase names collide; capitalised names hit the indirect-object trap (`Int $i` is `$i->Int` in perl -- irrelevant under the filter, but PPI lexes Word + Symbol either way).  PCL side: a statement-position DECLARATOR rule keyed on the SET the shim supplies (`use PCL::types qw(int num str)` -- data from the shim, mechanism generic), never on literal names in Pl/.
  Both spellings lower to the SAME fact vocabulary as #1035 (flagged :declared); choosing one is a USER decision when the task is scheduled.

SEMANTIC QUESTIONS TO RULE (unchanged from the first filing):
  - TRUSTED or CHECKED: a violated hint = undefined behaviour (perl's `use integer` precedent; the speed is the point) or an assertion at the binding site?  Suggested: trusted by default, PCL_CHECK_FACTS=1 asserts (shared with #1035's debug mode).
  - Box-model meaning: :int = raw fixnum slot (never a box), :num = double-float, :str = simple-string / str-buffer.  undef in an :int variable -- allowed as `(or null fixnum)` (weaker) or excluded?  Magic (tie, local, $1) on a hinted variable -> refuse LOUDLY (rule 12).
  - Aggregates: `my @a :int` = every element raw of that family (boxed-aggregates raw-element world, #841 family) -- phase 1 scalars only?
  - A sub RETURN type is a bigger feature (%p-leavesub would return the raw fixnum with no copy step) -- out of scope unless ruled in.
  - Registry: the hint is a Kind-A licensing SOURCE in Pl/Passes.pm so PCL_OPT=none still emits the general form and passes-01.t proves identical runs; a hint the compiler could ALSO prove is a no-op (byte-identical emission, guard row).

ACCEPTANCE (when scheduled): a bench row (fib / gcdrec shape) with and without hints; PCL_OPT=none run identical; real perl running the annotated file unchanged through the shim; the emitted fact block carrying the declared facts in the #1035 grammar.

RELATED: #1035 (part a, first), #75, #74, #995, docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md, docs/boxed-aggregates-design-s455.md.
subject: LOW PRIORITY / FUTURE (USER 2026-09-02) -- PART (b) of the IR-facts pair (#1035 is part a): USER-SUPPLIED type hints (int / num / str) on variable declarations and sub parameters, as an ATTRIBUTE (`my $i :int`) or as DISTINCT DECLARATORS (`int $i = 0`, USER-suggested) -- same fact vocabulary as #1035, flagged :declared; spelling is a USER decision when scheduled
